competences: The learner convert metres to centimetres and millimetres.
The learner convert centimetres to metres.
languageCompetence: Reads, pronounces, spells and correctly uses: metre, decimetre, centimetre, millimetre.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to convert metres to centimetres and millimetres.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to convert centimetres to metres.
priorKnowledge: Learners can multiply and divide by 100 and 1000.
materials: Metric length chart including dm, cm and mm
Ruler marked in centimetres and millimetres

steps.content: Learners can multiply and divide by 100 and 1000. Starter: Change 5 dm to centimetres.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher displays metric length chart including dm, cm and mm, reviews the prior skill, and asks: "Change 5 dm to centimetres." The teacher records learners’ methods and connects them to converting metric length units.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the previous skill, read the starter question, and explain which measurements or operations they would use.

steps.content: Metres and centimetres: $1\text{ m}=100\text{ cm}$. $1\text{ m}=1000\text{ mm}$. $100\text{ cm}=1\text{ m}$.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the following worked content: $1\text{ m}=100\text{ cm}$. $1\text{ m}=1000\text{ mm}$. $100\text{ cm}=1\text{ m}$. The teacher demonstrates each substitution or operation, asks learners to explain the units, and checks individual working before moving to the next step.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the given measurements, copy the calculation steps, explain the operation used, and check that the answer carries the correct units.

steps.content: Example: metres to centimetres: Convert $4\text{ m}$ to centimetres. $1\text{ m}=100\text{ cm}$. $4\text{ m}=4\times100\text{ cm}=400\text{ cm}$. Express $86\text{ m}$ as centimetres. $86\text{ m}=86\times100\text{ cm}$. $86\text{ m}=8600\text{ cm}$.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the following worked content: Convert $4\text{ m}$ to centimetres. $1\text{ m}=100\text{ cm}$. $4\text{ m}=4\times100\text{ cm}=400\text{ cm}$. Express $86\text{ m}$ as centimetres. $86\text{ m}=86\times100\text{ cm}$. $86\text{ m}=8600\text{ cm}$. The teacher demonstrates each substitution or operation, asks learners to explain the units, and checks individual working before moving to the next step.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the given measurements, copy the calculation steps, explain the operation used, and check that the answer carries the correct units.

steps.content: Example: centimetres to metres: Write $6200\text{ cm}$ as metres. $100\text{ cm}=1\text{ m}$. $6200\text{ cm}=6200\div100\text{ m}=62\text{ m}$. Change $530\text{ cm}$ to metres. $530\text{ cm}=530\div100\text{ m}$. $530\text{ cm}=5.3\text{ m}$.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the following worked content: Write $6200\text{ cm}$ as metres. $100\text{ cm}=1\text{ m}$. $6200\text{ cm}=6200\div100\text{ m}=62\text{ m}$. Change $530\text{ cm}$ to metres. $530\text{ cm}=530\div100\text{ m}$. $530\text{ cm}=5.3\text{ m}$. The teacher demonstrates each substitution or operation, asks learners to explain the units, and checks individual working before moving to the next step.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the given measurements, copy the calculation steps, explain the operation used, and check that the answer carries the correct units.

steps.content: Example: metres to millimetres: Change $7\text{ m}$ to millimetres. $1\text{ m}=1000\text{ mm}$. $7\text{ m}=7\times1000\text{ mm}$. $7\text{ m}=7000\text{ mm}$.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the following worked content: Change $7\text{ m}$ to millimetres. $1\text{ m}=1000\text{ mm}$. $7\text{ m}=7\times1000\text{ mm}$. $7\text{ m}=7000\text{ mm}$. The teacher demonstrates each substitution or operation, asks learners to explain the units, and checks individual working before moving to the next step.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the given measurements, copy the calculation steps, explain the operation used, and check that the answer carries the correct units.

steps.content: Change 5 dm to centimetres. Convert 8.5 m to millimetres. Convert 50 cm to metres. Express 86 m as centimetres. Change 530 cm to metres.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets these questions: Change 5 dm to centimetres. Convert 8.5 m to millimetres. Convert 50 cm to metres. Express 86 m as centimetres. Change 530 cm to metres. The teacher checks each learner’s working, marks against these computed answers: 5 × 10 = 50 cm. 8.5 × 1000 = 8500 mm. 50 ÷ 100 = 0.5 m. 86 × 100 = 8600 cm. 530 ÷ 100 = 5.3 m. and supports learners who confuse lengths, areas or units.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners solve the questions individually, show each calculation, compare marked answers, and correct any errors in substitution or units.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher asks learners to explain their solutions to these questions: Change 5 dm to centimetres. Convert 8.5 m to millimetres. Convert 50 cm to metres. Express 86 m as centimetres. Change 530 cm to metres. The teacher checks the lesson objectives against the written work and assigns correction of the final exercise item.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners explain their calculation methods, state the correct units, and correct the final exercise item after receiving feedback.

assessment: Mark the written working for these questions: Change 5 dm to centimetres. Convert 8.5 m to millimetres. Convert 50 cm to metres. Express 86 m as centimetres. Change 530 cm to metres. Check the stated measurements, operations, final answers and units against the answer key.
homework: Correct and fully work this exercise item: Change 530 cm to metres.
